title: After Success, with Pradeep Singh — Success: Part 3
summary: Pradeep Singh — a Harvard MBA, early Microsoft executive and serial founder, now 67 — sits with Kahran and Divya to look back at the audacious goals of his thirties and how they aged. He talks about the finiteness that arrives in your sixties, the anticlimax of hitting a milestone, the regret of having been too obsessed with work to be present with his kids ages 0–5, and how success now means competence, kindness and small days well lived.
topics: regret over missing your kids' early years
ego and arrogance after a career

intents.display: to hear a 67-year-old founder rethink what success was worth
to hear a father regret missing his kids when they were small
